note: Track guitar-melodies (guitar-scales), step 4: two positions of a major scale side by side, a tune that shifts from one to the next from the tab, the same tune on the neck view so the shift shows, then a tune that comes down the whole neck. The old tempo stages and Key choice are now moves (any key, 60 to 84 bpm), named only as {{=key}} and {{=bpm}}, so the third block is a new view of the tune in place of a key change. missing: the melody shape takes no position, so the tab decides where the shift falls and nothing marks it on the neck.

exercise.title: A tune that shifts position
exercise.why: A tune that climbs past the top of one position needs the next one, so you move your whole hand on one note and let the fingers fall on new frets.

cells.text:
The neck below frames two positions of the {{=key}} major scale that sit side by side, with the {{1}} notes ringed. Press Play below to hear the framed notes run up and back down, then play them yourself, from the lowest note up to the highest and back.
Practice until you can see where the lower position ends and the upper one starts.

Press Play below to start the backing track at {{=bpm}}, and play the tune from the tab. Most of it sits in the lower position: where the tab jumps up the neck, move your whole hand up and keep one finger to a fret.
If the shift comes late, play only the bar with the shift until your hand moves on time.
{{?bpm}}At a faster tempo the shift is still one move of the whole hand, on the same note.

Press Play below to start the backing track, and play the same tune again. This time it is drawn on the neck, so you can watch the note where the hand moves to the next position.
Practice until you move your hand before you look at the neck.
{{?key}}In another key the tune keeps its shape, but the shift can fall on another note: watch for it on the neck before you play.

Press Play below to start the backing track. This tune starts high and comes down the neck, so your hand shifts more than once.
Before each shift, look at the fret you are going to and not at your hand.
